# Steps

> Where the user is in a task of several steps, such as a checkout or a setup wizard, as a numbered list. Steps can be buttons that go back.

`<slab-steps>` · Navigation · built on `<ol> + aria-current="step"`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/steps/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/steps.js';
import 'slab-elements/steps.step.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-steps label="Checkout" step="2" navigable>
  <slab-steps-step>Cart</slab-steps-step>
  <slab-steps-step>Shipping</slab-steps-step>
  <slab-steps-step disabled>Payment</slab-steps-step>
</slab-steps>
```

Steps shows where the user is, not each step's content. Show the content for `step` yourself, and move along with `next()` and `previous()` from your own buttons, which don't dispatch "change". Setting `step` past the last Step makes every one complete, for when the task is done.

With `navigable`, each Step is a `<button>`, and clicking one sets `step` and dispatches "change". Set `disabled` on the Steps the user can't go to yet, such as those after the current one in a form that has to be filled in order. Without `navigable`, nothing in it is interactive.

The current Step has `aria-current="step"`, and each complete one has `complete-label` ("Completed" unless you set it) after its label, hidden visually, so screenreaders can tell it from an upcoming one. The number is hidden from them, since they read the list's own. A design's checkmark or color goes on `:state(complete)`, `:state(current)` and `:state(upcoming)`.

## Keyboard

| Key          | What it does                                                                      |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab          | In a `navigable` Steps, moves through the Steps' buttons, skipping disabled ones. |
| Enter, Space | On a Step's button, goes to that Step.                                            |

## Elements

### `<slab-steps>`

Import `slab-elements/steps.js` to register it.

Steps with no visual styles: where the user is in a task of several steps, such as a checkout or a setup wizard, as an `<ol>` of Steps.

Each Step gets an `<li>` of its own, as each link in a Breadcrumb does. The Steps before `step` are complete, the one at it is current and has `aria-current="step"`, and the rest are upcoming. Past the last Step, all of them are complete. A complete Step says so to screenreaders with `complete-label`, which is hidden visually.

Steps shows where the user is, not the steps' content. Show the content for `step` yourself, and call `next()` and `previous()` from your own buttons.

With `navigable`, each Step is a `<button>`, and clicking one sets `step` and dispatches "change". Disable the Steps the user can't go to yet, such as those after the current one in a form that has to be filled in order. Without it, nothing in Steps is interactive.

Style it through its parts, and each Step through its parts and `:state(complete)`, `:state(current)` and `:state(upcoming)`.

#### Attributes

| Name               | Type      | Default | Description                                                                                |
| ------------------ | --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `label` (required) | `string`  |         | Names the list.                                                                            |
| `complete-label`   | `string`  |         | Read by screenreaders after each complete Step's label. "Completed" in English when unset. |
| `navigable`        | `boolean` | `false` | Makes each Step a button that goes to it.                                                  |
| `step`             | `number`  | `1`     | The current Step, from 1. The Steps before it are complete.                                |

#### Properties

| Name                | Type     | Description          |
| ------------------- | -------- | -------------------- |
| `steps` (read-only) | `Step[]` | Its Steps, in order. |

#### Methods

| Signature          | Description                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `next(): void`     | Goes to the next Step, or past the last one, where every Step is complete. It doesn't dispatch "change", which is only for the user's clicks. |
| `previous(): void` | Goes to the previous Step, stopping at the first. It doesn't dispatch "change", which is only for the user's clicks.                          |

#### Events

| Name     | Type    | Description                                                                                      |
| -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `change` | `Event` | When the user goes to another Step. Setting `step`, `next()` and `previous()` don't dispatch it. |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type   | Description         |
| --------- | ------ | ------------------- |
| (default) | `Step` | The Steps, in order |

#### CSS parts

| Name   | Description           |
| ------ | --------------------- |
| `item` | Each Step's list item |
| `list` | The Steps             |

### `<slab-steps-step>`

Import `slab-elements/steps.step.js` to register it.

A Step with no visual styles: one step of its Steps, with a number, a label and an optional description.

Its Steps numbers it and tells it whether it's complete, current or upcoming. The current one has `aria-current="step"`, and a complete one has its Steps' `complete-label` after its label, hidden visually, so screenreaders say so. The number is hidden from screenreaders, which read the list's own.

In a `navigable` Steps, `::part(step)` is a `<button>`, and clicking it goes to the Step. Set `disabled` on Steps the user can't go to yet.

Style it through its parts and `:state(complete)`, `:state(current)`, `:state(upcoming)` and, in a `navigable` Steps, `:state(navigable)`.

#### Attributes

| Name       | Type      | Default | Description                                             |
| ---------- | --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Keeps the user from going to it in a `navigable` Steps. |

#### Properties

| Name            | Type                                    | Description                             |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `completeLabel` | `string`                                | Set by its Steps.                       |
| `index`         | `number`                                | Its position, from 1. Set by its Steps. |
| `navigable`     | `boolean`                               | Set by its Steps.                       |
| `status`        | `'complete' \| 'current' \| 'upcoming'` | Set by its Steps.                       |

#### Slots

| Name          | Type                | Description           |
| ------------- | ------------------- | --------------------- |
| `description` | `Element \| string` | Shown below the label |
| (default)     | `Element \| string` | The label             |

#### CSS parts

| Name          | Description                                                         |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `description` | Holds the description                                               |
| `indicator`   | The Step's number, hidden from screenreaders                        |
| `label`       | Holds the label                                                     |
| `status`      | Its Steps' complete label, hidden visually, on a complete Step      |
| `step`        | The number, label and status. A button when its Steps is navigable. |

#### CSS states

| Name                | Description                                            |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `:state(complete)`  | While its `status` is "complete".                      |
| `:state(current)`   | While its `status` is "current".                       |
| `:state(disabled)`  | While it's disabled.                                   |
| `:state(navigable)` | While its Steps is `navigable`, so it can be moved to. |
| `:state(upcoming)`  | While its `status` is "upcoming".                      |
